title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Cross-Tenant Orchestrated Migration
summary: Hold: the batch automation entry contains an English instruction inside a PowerShell command, so it cannot be run as printed. The page also assigns a default and licensing model to the future admin-center experience without establishing that the existing tools' configuration and licensing apply to it. The roadmap facts and the separately described workload commands were verified; the earlier fetch warnings did not recur.

Cross-Tenant Orchestrated Migration moves Microsoft 365 user and shared data between tenants.
claims.quote: Cross-Tenant Orchestrated Migration for User Data Migration (UDM) and Shared Data Migration (SDM) allows customers to move their Microsoft 365 data from one Microsoft tenant to another.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The documented Migration Orchestrator automatically sequences supported workloads.
claims.quote: The Migration Orchestrator handles sequencing automatically for supported workloads.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents individual cross-tenant tools for mailbox, OneDrive and SharePoint migration.
claims.quote: Individual workload migration | Migrating a single workload, or when you need granular control over each workload's timeline | Cross-tenant tools (mailbox, OneDrive, SharePoint)

claims.claim: Mergers, divestitures and consolidation are common tenant-migration scenarios.
claims.quote:
Merger or acquisition: Your organization acquired another company, and you need to consolidate users and data into a single tenant.
Divestiture or spin-off: A business unit is being separated, and users need to move to a new or existing tenant owned by another organization.

claims.claim: The documented Cross Tenant User Data Migration licence is a per-user, one-time-fee add-on.
claims.quote: Cross-Tenant migrations require a per-user license (one-time fee) and can be assigned on either the source or target user object. This license enables the migration of all content supported by orchestration. Cross Tenant User Data Migration is available as an add-on

claims.claim: The migration licence can be assigned to either the source or target user.
claims.quote: Cross-Tenant migrations require a per-user license (one-time fee) and can be assigned on either the source or target user object.

claims.claim: Migration fails if the proper migration licence is not assigned.
claims.quote: If you don't have the proper license assigned to the user being migrated, the migration fails

claims.claim: Administrators in both source and target tenants participate in migration setup.
claims.quote: To establish trust, each SharePoint tenant administrator must run specific commands on both source and target tenants.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for validating and running an orchestrator migration batch.
claims.quote: Searched: "migration orchestrator" "admin center" migration batch UI. Opened Running the migration and reviewed search results; the orchestrator uses Graph/PowerShell, while returned Exchange UI instructions concern different migration types.

claims.claim: The displayed Connect/Test/once-the-status-is-ValidatePassed/Move sequence is a runnable PowerShell call.
claims.quote:
Test-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <batch display name or job id>
Once the batch status is ValidatePassed, call migrate to start the actual migration.
Move-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <batch display name or job id>
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api.call to "Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'CrossTenantContentMigration.ReadWrite.All'; Test-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <id>". Move the English instruction out of the call and append to the existing note: "After the batch status reaches ValidatePassed, run Move-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <id>." Apply the same change to the rendered row. The cited Learn page documents validation and migration as separate steps, not an inline 'once' command.

claims.claim: Orchestrator migration commands run from the target tenant as Microsoft 365 Migration Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: All commands below are run through Microsoft Graph from the target tenant by Microsoft M365 Migration Administrators or Global Administrators. Source tenants cannot run the migration commands.

claims.claim: The maximum orchestrator batch size is 100 users.
claims.quote: The maximum batch size is 100 users.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for the SharePoint and OneDrive cross-tenant migration trust.
claims.quote: Searched: "cross-tenant" "trust" "SharePoint admin center" migration. Opened SharePoint trust step 2; read OneDrive trust step 2 search excerpts. Both specify Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship on the two tenants, not an admin-center path.

claims.claim: The source tenant establishes trust using Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship with Scenario MnA, PartnerRole Target and the target host URL.
claims.quote:
On the source tenant, run this command to send a trust request to the target tenant:
Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship -Scenario MnA -PartnerRole Target -PartnerCrossTenantHostUrl <TARGETCrossTenantHostUrl>

claims.claim: The target tenant must also run Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship with Scenario MnA, PartnerRole Source and the source host URL.
claims.quote:
On the target tenant, run this command to send a trust request to the source tenant:
Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship -Scenario MnA -PartnerRole Source -PartnerCrossTenantHostUrl <SOURCECrossTenantHostUrl>

claims.claim: No control for the roadmap admin-center page is documented; the existing orchestrator documentation describes Graph operations instead.
claims.quote: Searched: "migration orchestrator" "admin center" migration batch UI; "Cross-Tenant Orchestrated Migration" licensing pricing admin center. Opened orchestrator overview and Running the migration; neither documents the roadmap admin-center page or a separate control for it.

claims.claim: The documented orchestrator is managed through Graph APIs usable from PowerShell or Graph Explorer.
claims.quote: Migrations are managed through Graph APIs. These APIs can be run with PowerShell 5 or 7, or with Graph Explorer.

claims.claim: The standalone OneDrive and SharePoint tools use SharePoint Online PowerShell and the SharePoint Online Management Shell.
claims.quote: Microsoft SharePoint Online Powershell. Confirm you have the most recent version installed. Download SharePoint Online Management Shell from the official Microsoft Download Center.

claims.claim: Validation results expire after seven days.
claims.quote: Validation results expire after seven days. If more than seven days pass between validation passing and calling migrate, you must revalidate the batch before migration can proceed.

claims.claim: The roadmap admin-center experience has a documented admin-opt-in default.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cross-Tenant Orchestrated Migration" "enable" "default". Read roadmap, orchestrator overview, Running the migration and tenant-configuration search excerpt. Existing tools require admin setup; none states the new admin-center experience's default on arrival.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to "unknown" and state "Microsoft has not stated the default for the roadmap admin-center experience." Do not transfer the existing script-based orchestrator's setup requirements to the future experience without a source connecting them.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The page consistently establishes add-on licensing for the roadmap experience.
claims.quote:
licensing: model: "add-on"
That describes the existing tool; final licensing for the roadmap experience is not yet published.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "unknown". Prefix licensing.notes with "For the existing tools: " so the verified User Data Migration and Shared Data Migration licence details remain explicitly separate from the unpublished licensing for the roadmap experience.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every governance-checklist control is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote:
Plan identity mapping, licences in the target tenant and holds.
Precreate target security groups, populate memberships and include them in identity mapping before migrating content.
Verify group memberships and permissions, and decommission source content per policy.
claims.fix: The Before rollout steps for identity mapping, licence assignment, holds and group preparation, and the After rollout step for group memberships and permissions, name controls without corresponding table rows. Narrow those checklist steps to planning and reconciliation advice rather than instructions to configure or check controls the table does not cover.
